chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), 'A man swore by disavowal from Allah and from His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), then he reneged. What is his repentance and his expiation?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should feed ten poor people, for each poor person a handful, and he should seek forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath of disavowal from Allah and the Messenger?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Hadi (AS) specifies the expiation (kaffarah) for breaking an oath of disavowal, prescribing feeding ten poor people with one mud of food each alongside seeking forgiveness. This ruling aligns with the general principle of kaffarah for broken oaths but highlights the specific measure of 'mud' and the dual requirement of material charity and spiritual repentance. The emphasis on feeding the poor underscores the social dimension of oath-breaking in Shia jurisprudence, linking personal accountability to community welfare.
